records.claim: Subclass 189 is a points-tested skilled visa route. SkillSelect requires an expression of interest; the applicant must nominate an occupation available to the visa, provide English and skills-assessment information, and meet or exceed the 65-point threshold for invitation eligibility. Meeting 65 points does not guarantee an invitation.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Department of Home Affairs SkillSelect guidance; scope is limited to subclass 189 and does not infer subclass 190 or 491 eligibility.

records.claim: The reviewed current SkillSelect guidance establishes the points threshold and application workflow but does not establish a separate visa-specific proof-of-funds threshold for subclass 189. Financial-verification treatment remains an explicit research gap and must not be inferred from another Australian visa stream.
records.methodology: Negative finding from the exact official SkillSelect source reviewed; retained as a research-gap record rather than a proof-of-funds claim.

records.claim: For subclass 189, the applicant submits an expression of interest through SkillSelect, may receive an invitation, and after invitation has 60 days to submit the visa application online through ImmiAccount. The occupation must be on the applicable skilled occupation list.
records.methodology: Direct review of the current official EOI workflow; no invitation probability or processing-time claim is inferred.

records.claim: The SMC Points-based pathway requires 6 skilled resident points, with points available from qualification, occupational registration or income and, where applicable, skilled work experience in New Zealand. Applicants must also satisfy the common SMC requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of the current SMC visa page; the record is scoped to the Points-based child route and does not inherit evidence from the NZ-skilled umbrella.

records.claim: Current SMC guidance requires qualifying skilled employment or a job offer from an accredited employer and payment at the applicable SMC wage threshold. The current operations guidance records a median-wage threshold of NZD 35.00 per hour for ANZSCO skill levels 1-3 and 1.5 times median wage for ANZSCO skill levels 4-5 or occupations not included in ANZSCO.
records.methodology: Direct review of current SMC operations guidance; wage treatment is recorded as a route eligibility condition, not as a general cost-of-living or proof-of-funds estimate.

records.claim: Applicants submit an expression of interest and, if accepted, are invited to apply for the SMC Resident Visa. Applications must be assessed under the pathway for which the invitation was issued, subject to applicable transitional rules.
records.methodology: Direct review of current SMC operational instructions, including the EOI/invitation process and transitional treatment.

records.claim: The Skilled Work Experience pathway requires at least 5 years of directly relevant work experience, including at least 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand, together with the common SMC requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of the current SMC visa page; exact child-route scope is preserved.

records.claim: The Skilled Work Experience pathway is subject to the SMC skilled-employment wage settings. Current operations guidance specifies at least the applicable median wage for ANZSCO skill levels 1-3, with higher wage treatment for ANZSCO skill levels 4-5 or roles outside ANZSCO; pathway-specific exceptions can apply under current SMC instructions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current skilled-employment instructions; this is a wage eligibility condition, not a proof-of-funds claim.

records.claim: The Skilled Work Experience pathway is selected through the SMC EOI and invitation process. The residence application must be made under the pathway stated in the invitation and satisfy the evidence requirements applicable to that pathway.
records.methodology: Direct review of current SMC operational instructions; no parent-route inheritance is used.

records.claim: The Trades and Technician pathway requires work in a specified eligible trade or technician occupation, a relevant Level 4 or higher qualification, and at least 4 years of directly relevant post-qualification experience including at least 18 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand.
records.methodology: Direct review of current SMC visa guidance and the August 2026 pathway settings; exact occupation-list validation remains a separate promotion gate.

records.claim: The Trades and Technician pathway requires the applicant's skilled New Zealand work to meet the SMC median-wage setting applicable to the pathway. Current INZ guidance states the median wage is NZD 35.00 per hour and confirms wage maintenance rules for the pathway.
records.methodology: Direct review of current INZ pathway-change guidance; wage threshold is treated as route eligibility rather than proof of settlement funds.

records.claim: The Trades and Technician pathway uses the SMC EOI and invitation workflow and requires evidence of the eligible occupation, relevant qualification and post-qualification work experience when the residence application is assessed.
records.methodology: Direct review of current SMC application evidence guidance; qualification and occupation verification remain explicit child-route gates.

records.claim: Austria's Other Key Workers route is an exact Red-White-Red Card category for third-country citizens taking up key-worker employment. Eligibility includes the labour-market test and a minimum of 55 points under the published qualification, work-experience, age, language and other criteria.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official Other Key Workers category page; evidence is not generalized to other Red-White-Red categories.

records.claim: For 2026, the prospective employer must pay the statutory minimum of EUR 3,465 gross per month for the Other Key Workers category.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official category page; amount is recorded as the route's statutory salary floor, not an estimate of living costs.

records.claim: A qualifying third-country national may apply for a Red-White-Red Card valid for 24 months under the Other Key Workers category; continued eligibility can support a Red-White-Red Card plus after at least 21 months of qualifying employment during the preceding 24 months, subject to the competent authority's assessment.
records.methodology: Direct review of the official Other Key Workers process/category guidance.

records.claim: The 2026 Flussi programme authorizes 76,200 entries for non-seasonal subordinate employment. The route is quota-controlled and applies to the sectors, worker categories and territorial allocations specified by the 2026 programming decree and implementing guidance.
records.methodology: Direct review of current official 2026 Flussi quota guidance; scope is limited to non-seasonal subordinate work and does not generalize to autonomous or seasonal routes.

records.claim: The 2026 official Flussi materials require the employment relationship and contractual conditions to satisfy the applicable immigration and labour-law requirements, but the reviewed quota guidance does not establish a single route-wide salary figure. Exact compensation validation remains tied to the applicable sector, contract and employer documentation.
records.methodology: Conservative field-level finding from the official 2026 Flussi guidance; no universal salary threshold is invented.

records.claim: For 2026 non-seasonal subordinate work, employers use the ALI portal to submit the nulla osta request. Pre-compilation ran before the click day, and non-seasonal subordinate applications were scheduled for 16 February 2026, with applications possible through 31 December 2026 subject to quota availability. Employer-side labour-market availability verification and supporting documentation are part of the process where applicable.
records.methodology: Direct review of current 2026 Flussi operational guidance and official labour-market verification guidance; quota and employer-side gates remain explicit.
